title: Impact of Additional Representative on Public Spending

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).
- Why: Districts are assigned a second representative when the running variable (population) crosses a known threshold. Near the threshold, assignment is as-good-as-random, and comparing units just above vs. just below identifies the local causal effect on public spending per capita.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff: in the absence of treatment, expected public spending per capita varies smoothly with population at the threshold.
  - No precise manipulation of the running variable around the cutoff.
  - SUTVA and local overlap around the cutoff.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis (sharp local polynomial RDD)
# - Prints a clear numerical result (treatment effect at cutoff)
# - Includes basic robustness checks (bandwidths, polynomial order, donut, placebo cutoffs)

# 1) Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s99_data.csv")

# Inspect basic structure
stopifnot(all(c("running_var","treated","y") %in% names(df)))
df <- df[!is.na(df$running_var) & !is.na(df$y), ]

# 2) Define cutoff
# The data are scaled 0-1 and treated=1 appears above the midpoint in the preview,
# so we use c = 0.5 as the assignment threshold.
c <- 0.5

# 3) Helper functions for local RDD using base R (triangular kernel, sharp design)
tri_weight <- function(z, h) {
  w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(z)/h)
  w[abs(z) > h] <- 0
  return(w)
}

fit_local_rdd <- function(y, x, c, h, p = 1, donut = 0) {
  z <- x - c
  keep <- abs(z) <= h & abs(z) >= donut
  yk <- y[keep]; zk <- z[keep]; Dk <- as.integer(zk >= 0)
  wk <- tri_weight(zk, h)
  # Guard for too few observations
  if (sum(keep) < 30 || sum(keep & zk < 0) < 10 || sum(keep & zk >= 0) < 10) {
    return(list(est=NA, se=NA, n=sum(keep), h=h, p=p, donut=donut))
  }
  if (p == 1) {
    dat <- data.frame(y=yk, D=Dk, z=zk)
    fit <- lm(y ~ D + z + D:z, data=dat, weights=wk)
    cf <- summary(fit)$coef
    est <- cf["D","Estimate"]; se <- cf["D","Std. Error"]
  } else if (p == 2) {
    dat <- data.frame(y=yk, D=Dk, z=zk, z2=zk^2)
    fit <- lm(y ~ D + z + z2 + D:z + D:z2, data=dat, weights=wk)
    cf <- summary(fit)$coef
    est <- cf["D","Estimate"]; se <- cf["D","Std. Error"]
  } else {
    stop("Only p=1 or p=2 implemented")
  }
  list(est=as.numeric(est), se=as.numeric(se), n=sum(keep), h=h, p=p, donut=donut)
}

print_result <- function(res, label) {
  if (is.na(res$est)) {
    cat(sprintf("%s: insufficient data within bandwidth h=%.3f (n=%d)\n", label, res$h, res$n))
  } else {
    ci_l <- res$est - 1.96*res$se
    ci_u <- res$est + 1.96*res$se
    cat(sprintf(
      "%s: tau_hat=%.4f, SE=%.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], n=%d, h=%.3f, p=%d, donut=%.3f\n",
      label, res$est, res$se, ci_l, ci_u, res$n, res$h, res$p, res$donut
    ))
  }
}

# 4) Choose a practical bandwidth baseline relative to support length
rng <- range(df$running_var, na.rm=TRUE)
support_len <- diff(rng)
# Start with 20% of support; adjust if too few obs
base_h <- 0.20 * support_len
if (base_h <= 0) base_h <- 0.10

# Diagnostics: Sharpness of the design (alignment of treated with running_var >= c)
D_true <- as.integer(df$running_var >= c)
if ("treated" %in% names(df)) {
  concord <- mean(D_true == df$treated, na.rm=TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("Design sharpness (share treated == 1[x>=c]): %.3f\n", concord))
} else {
  cat("No 'treated' column provided for sharpness diagnostic; proceeding with sharp RDD.\n")
}

# 5) Main estimate: local linear (p=1), triangular kernel, baseline bandwidth
main_res <- fit_local_rdd(df$y, df$running_var, c=c, h=base_h, p=1, donut=0)
print_result(main_res, "Main RDD (local linear)")

# 6) Robustness checks

# 6a) Bandwidth sensitivity (smaller and larger)
bw_small <- 0.75 * base_h
bw_large <- 1.50 * base_h
res_bw_small <- fit_local_rdd(df$y, df$running_var, c=c, h=bw_small, p=1, donut=0)
res_bw_large <- fit_local_rdd(df$y, df$running_var, c=c, h=bw_large, p=1, donut=0)
print_result(res_bw_small, "Bandwidth 0.75x")
print_result(res_bw_large, "Bandwidth 1.50x")

# 6b) Polynomial order (quadratic, p=2)
res_quad <- fit_local_rdd(df$y, df$running_var, c=c, h=base_h, p=2, donut=0)
print_result(res_quad, "Quadratic (p=2)")

# 6c) Donut RDD (exclude tight window around cutoff)
donut_width <- 0.02 * support_len
res_donut <- fit_local_rdd(df$y, df$running_var, c=c, h=base_h, p=1, donut=donut_width)
print_result(res_donut, "Donut (exclude |x-c|<2% of support)")

# 6d) Placebo cutoffs (where no policy change should occur)
placebos <- c(0.30, 0.70)
for (pc in placebos) {
  # Ensure placebo is inside support
  if (pc > rng[1] + 0.05*support_len && pc < rng[2] - 0.05*support_len) {
    res_pl <- fit_local_rdd(df$y, df$running_var, c=pc, h=base_h, p=1, donut=0)
    print_result(res_pl, sprintf("Placebo cutoff c=%.2f", pc))
  }
}

# 7) Clear numerical result (restate main)
if (!is.na(main_res$est)) {
  ci_l <- main_res$est - 1.96*main_res$se
  ci_u <- main_res$est + 1.96*main_res$se
  cat("\n==== Summary: Main Causal Estimate at the Threshold ====\n")
  cat(sprintf("Treatment effect on public spending per capita at c=%.2f: %.4f\n", c, main_res$est))
  cat(sprintf("Standard error: %.4f; 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", main_res$se, ci_l, ci_u))
  cat(sprintf("Bandwidth h=%.3f; Local polynomial order p=%d; Sample size used n=%d\n",
              main_res$h, main_res$p, main_res$n))
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Gaining a second representative likely raises political influence and bargaining power for the district, leading to higher per-capita public spending around the threshold.
- Magnitude: Given variables appear scaled roughly between 0 and 1, I expect a local treatment effect on the order of +0.10 to +0.25 in y near the cutoff, with robustness to reasonable bandwidth and polynomial choices. The donut and placebo checks should not overturn the positive effect, and placebo cutoffs should yield near-zero estimates.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the population threshold for a second representative as a cutoff for treatment assignment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The presence of a second representative decreases public spending per capita.
